title: Do Not Fear, God Is With You

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When you go to war against your enemies and see horses and chariots and an army greater than yours, do not be afraid of them, because the Lord your God, who brought you up out of Egypt, will be with you. - Deut 20:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As Israel faced the prospect of war, God knew exactly what would frighten them, an enemy with more horses, more chariots, and a bigger army. Fear would be the natural response. So God speaks directly to that fear, "do not be afraid of them." And He gives the reason, not that Israel was strong, but that the Lord who rescued them from Egypt would be with them.

This is so important to notice. God does not tell them to be brave because of their own strength or numbers. He tells them not to fear because of His presence. Their courage was to rest entirely on the God who had already proven His power by delivering them from Egypt. The One who split the sea would not abandon them now.

We face our own overwhelming "armies", fears about health, finances, relationships, or the future. And God speaks the same word to us, do not be afraid, because He is with us. This is not empty comfort. In Christ, God has given us the greatest proof of His commitment, His own Son. The One who did not spare His Son will surely be with us in every battle (Rom 8:31-32). Our courage rests not in our circumstances but in His presence. What "greater army" are you facing today that God is telling you not to fear?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What overwhelming "army" are you facing right now?
2. Where is your courage resting, in your strength or God's presence?
3. How does God's past faithfulness steady you today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when I face things far bigger than me, remind me that You are with me. Let my courage rest not in myself but in You. Amen.
